title: Nectar de pastèque (Watermelon Drink)
author: Tata Ngome et al. (CIFOR-ICRAF, IRAD, Université de Ngaoundéré)
desc: Two large watermelons soaked 5 minutes in water with a little bleach, peeled, cut, crushed, pressed and filtered; water and sugar added and boiled 10 minutes, cooled and bottled.
longDesc: p. 78 of the October 2023 recipe book: 2 large watermelons, 500 g sugar and 3 litres of water, with an optional preservative. Method as the mango drink: bleach soak 5 minutes, peel and cut, crush and press, filter, add water and sugar and boil 10 minutes, cool, add the preservative, bottle, keep cool. The size of the ‘large’ watermelons is not quantified; the diagram shows 70 °C for 5 minutes.
ingredients: A little bleach (javel) for the soak — quantity not printed
steps: Soak in drinking water with a little bleach for 5 minutes.
Peel and cut. Crush and press. Filter.
Add the water and sugar. Boil 10 minutes.
chefTips: The page prints no doneness cue beyond the boil time.
The diagram shows 70 °C for 5 minutes against 10 minutes in the text.
The bleach quantity is not printed.
commonMistakes: Leaving the seeds in the press.
storage: Keep cool. No shelf life is printed.
culturalNote: The book attributes its recipes to the northern part of Cameroon and names no community, lamidat or town for any recipe.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Nectar de pastèque’ (p. 78). Authors as printed: ‘Tata Ngome et al.’ (CIFOR-ICRAF, IRAD, Université de Ngaoundéré; ReSI-NoC project); October 2023 (V1), © 2024, CC BY 4.0. Yield not printed for any recipe in the book. Servings 15 is a placeholder. TWO-PASS.
CONFLICT (unreconciled): diagram ‘Cuisson (70°, 5min)’ vs 10 minutes in the text. ABSENT: bleach and preservative quantities; watermelon size; shelf life.
